title: Recursion, stack overflow, and tail calls
hook: Every recursive call pushes a new frame onto the call stack. JavaScript engines enforce a maximum stack size — deep recursion throws RangeError, and tail-call optimization is not something you can rely on in practice.

blocks.text: **Recursion** is when a function calls itself to solve a smaller subproblem. Each call adds a **stack frame** with local variables and the return address. When the stack exceeds the engine limit, you get **stack overflow** (RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded). **Tail-call optimization** (TCO) would reuse the current frame when the recursive call is the final action — it is in the ECMAScript spec but not implemented in V8, JavaScriptCore, or SpiderMonkey for general cases.

Reusing the current stack frame when a function's last action is calling another function.

entries.plainDefinition: The condition that stops recursion and starts returning values up the stack.

blocks.text: Tree traversal, JSON parsing, and divide-and-conquer algorithms use recursion naturally — but depth 10,000 on Node.js will crash. Interviews test whether you can rewrite to an iterative loop or an explicit stack. Confusing call stack with scope chain causes wrong answers about closures (covered earlier). Async recursion via `setTimeout` or `queueMicrotask` does not grow the stack synchronously — a trick for deferring deep walks without overflow.

blocks.title: Do not rely on TCO in JavaScript
blocks.body: Only Safari ever shipped limited TCO. V8 explicitly does not. Write iterative solutions for unbounded depth.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Enter function
items.body: Push frame with parameters and locals onto call stack.

items.title: Hit base case or recurse
items.body: Base case returns a value. Recursive case calls self with smaller input.

items.title: Stack grows
items.body: Each pending call waits until deeper calls return — frames accumulate.

items.title: Unwind
items.body: Returns bubble up, popping frames until the original caller resumes.

snippet.explanation: Line 1: infinite sync recursion — no base case. Engine throws when stack limit hit, typically ~10k–50k frames depending on host.

blocks.title: Assuming tail-recursive code is stack-safe
blocks.body: function fact(n, acc=1) { return n<=1 ? acc : fact(n-1, n*acc); } still overflows in V8 for large n. Use a loop.

blocks.title: Mixing up call stack and scope chain
blocks.body: Deep recursion blows the call stack. Closures retain environments on the heap — different memory concern.

interviewTakeaways: Each recursive call pushes a stack frame; missing base case → RangeError stack overflow.
JavaScript engines do not implement practical TCO — iterative or explicit-stack solutions for unbounded depth.
Call stack tracks execution; scope chain tracks variable lookup — related but distinct.
60s: Recursion = self-call + base case. Stack grows per pending call. V8 no TCO. Rewrite to loop or explicit stack for production depth.
Follow-up: traverse a DOM tree without blowing the stack.
commonPitfalls: Claiming tail-call optimization saves you in Node.js — it does not in V8.
Using recursion for unbounded user input depth — denial-of-service risk on server.
Strong answer: 'Sync recursion costs stack frames. Base case required. Prefer iteration for unknown depth. Defer with microtasks only when async semantics are acceptable.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: C# also throws StackOverflowException on unbounded sync recursion. Neither CLR nor V8 offers reliable TCO for interview-grade answers.
TypeScript can express recursive types (JSON, trees). Runtime recursion limits still apply to the JavaScript call stack.
